tr-message: Choose a firmware distribution and build service, then select your device and version.
tr-customize: Customize installed packages and/or first boot script
tr-dtb-help: Device tree blob. This file configures the Linux Kernel for the hardware.
tr-uboot-help: Bootloader image. Low-level software which loads the operating system early on boot.
tr-cpximg-help: Use with sysupgrade in the stock firmware or with the built-in cpximg loader.
tr-eva-help: Image with firmware and a boot loader.
tr-factory-help: Use a Factory image for an initial installation from the device's original firmware. Follow the installation instructions for your device.
tr-sysupgrade-help: Use a Sysupgrade image to update a compatible existing installation through LuCI or the terminal. Follow your device's upgrade instructions when changing distributions.
tr-kernel-help: Linux kernel as a separate image.
tr-initramfs-help: Linux kernel with minimal file system. Useful for first installation or recovery.
tr-rootfs-help: Root file system as a separate image.
tr-sdcard-help: Image that is meant to be flashed onto a SD-Card.
tr-tftp-help: TFTP images are used to flash a device via the TFTP method of the bootloader.
tr-defaults: Script to run on first boot (uci-defaults)
tr-uci-drafts-help: Drafts are kept separately for each firmware distribution in this page. Build services for the same distribution share its draft. Reloading the page clears the drafts.
tr-rootfs-size-help: Leave empty for the device default. The allowed range follows the selected service. This depends on the device image layout and does not increase physical storage.
tr-rootfs-invalid: Enter a whole number within the selected service's size range, or leave it empty.
tr-asu-service-help: Changing distribution or service reloads devices, versions and default packages. Script drafts are restored per distribution. Advanced options are retained; check that custom feeds match the selected distribution. Selection is locked while a build is running.
tr-repositories-help: Enter a unique name and an HTTP(S) feed directory URL for the selected distribution. Version and platform placeholders are supported. The build service may restrict allowed feeds.
tr-repositories-mode-help: Append keeps the build server's existing feeds. Replace uses only the feeds listed below; include every feed needed by your packages.
tr-repository-name-invalid: Enter a feed name using letters, numbers, underscores, dots or hyphens.
tr-repository-name-duplicate: Each feed must have a different name.
tr-repository-url-invalid: Enter a complete HTTP or HTTPS feed URL. Check any placeholders.
tr-repository-keys-help: Paste one complete feed signing public key per entry, preserving line breaks (for example, a usign public key). The build server verifies the key format.
